offers_products.reason: Sells no goods; hotel stays and food are part of lodging services.

offers_services.reason: Lodging REIT whose hotels and resorts provide rooms and hospitality; REITs count as services.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Hotel and resort guests, including leisure travelers at Hilton Hawaiian Village and Casa Marina, are individuals.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Hotels in business districts and conference destinations serve corporate travelers, groups and conventions.

recurring_revenue.reason: Revenue comes from nightly room bookings and hotel spending, not contracts or subscriptions; repeat guests are not assured.

cyclical_demand.reason: Leisure and business travel and conference stays at luxury and upper upscale hotels are easily cut in downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Hotel room stays are small, frequent purchases relative to guests' spending.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for hotel properties and brands; the company owns real estate and operators supply staff.

large_customers.reason: Guests are mainly individual leisure and business travelers; groups exist but households and travelers dominate.

asset_heavy.reason: Owns 29 hotels and resorts with about 21,000 rooms; lodging REIT needing ongoing property capital investment.

notes: Lodging REIT; hotels run by brand and third-party operators. Guest mix between leisure and business or group travelers is uncertain.
